title: Build-up Numerical Disadvantage
definition: The tactical failure to create a numerical advantage in the defensive third during build-up, often caused by a goalkeeper who cannot distribute under pressure or a lack of wide support.
content: This concept describes a critical vulnerability in the initial phase of possession where a team fails to generate a local numerical superiority against the opponent's press. A primary cause is a goalkeeper who lacks the technical ability to act as a third center-back, forcing the team to rely on center-backs who may be under pressure. When the goalkeeper cannot participate effectively, the team often defaults to a 2v2 or 3v3 situation in the defensive third, which is easily neutralized by high-intensity pressing. Furthermore, if fullbacks are not committed forward or are out of position, the width is lost, compressing the space for the center-backs. This forces midfielders to drop deep to receive, which reduces the team's presence in the final third and limits creative options. The result is a stagnant build-up where the team struggles to progress the ball, leading to long balls or turnovers in dangerous areas. To fix this, teams must ensure the goalkeeper is involved in the build-up or that fullbacks provide immediate width to create passing lanes and numerical advantages, allowing the team to bypass the initial press effectively.
